results.summary: Four static checks implemented as registered detectors, each with positive fixtures in corpus/src/bad, negative controls in corpus/src/good, finding-level assertions, and a DETECTORS.md section stating what it finds and misses. HS-03 `hookrisk-admin-surface` (class admin-surface): High when a public/external mutator writes a non-mapping state variable the callbacks read (or calls updateDynamicLPFee) with no caller restriction; Medium when the same is owner/role-gated, listing the callback-read variables it writes. Access control is structural via a new `access_guard`: a sender-vs-authority comparison (state var, address(this), non-zero constant, owner()-style callee) or a role lookup keyed by the sender that decides a branch/require without arithmetic — this recognises OpenZeppelin AccessControl by behaviour, and `hasOwnerOnlyFunctions` now reports true on StablePairHook. HS-05 `hookrisk-external-call-in-swap-path` (Medium): `classify_destination` sorts swap-path calls into PoolManager / library / own-currency (Currency-typed or unwrapped key.currency0/1) / third-party; one finding per destination with metrics {destination, isStatic, unhandled}, plus new profile metric externalCallsInSwapPathThirdParty next to the raw count. HS-06 `hookrisk-unbounded-dynamic-fee` (Medium): traces updateDynamicLPFee's fee argument and beforeSwap's lpFeeOverride (OVERRIDE_FEE_FLAG on the chain) back through overrides, setters, struct/mapping reads and abi.decode; bounded by a comparison against a constant/immutable, a constant mask, LPFeeLibrary.validate/isValid, or min(); message names the sources. HS-02 third case (Medium, discriminator = field): a declared returns-delta flag whose callback returns 0/ZERO_DELTA on every fully-lifted path; silent on computed deltas and on partially lifted delegates (which is how HR-E205 made it accuse OZ AntiSandwich at first). `_report` gained a per-finding `impact` override so one rule class carries both HS-03 severities. Schema: `metrics` now has two shapes keyed by `dependentRequired`, and the enum gains the harness classes unvalidated-pool-key and callback-selector-mismatch for agent H. Makefile bad gate requires a High and a Medium. Also fixed a pre-existing detector-test failure (disabled-callback wording drifted in 81de757) that made the baseline `make test` exit 2.

results.summary:
Wired the research-adopted rule classes into the taxonomy, scoring, schema, SARIF and the report, and wrote the documentation.

TYPES: RuleClass gains `unvalidated-pool-key` (added to CLASSIFICATION_CLASSES: INFO, gate-exempt, scores nothing) and `callback-selector-mismatch` (HIGH defect, deliberately NOT a classification).

SCORING: `admin-surface`, `external-call-in-swap-path`, `unbounded-dynamic-fee` moved into IMPLEMENTED_CLASSES; `autonomousParameterUpdates` left NEVER_MEASURED and is now raised by admin-surface (2 for the HIGH unguarded shape, 1 for the MEDIUM owner-only shape), externalDependencies by external-call-in-swap-path (2, or 1 when the finding's metrics.isStatic is true, 2 when the metric is absent), priceImpactingBehavior keeps 2 for unbounded-dynamic-fee. Because the score depends on the finding's shape and not only its class, the mapping is data, not code: a new per-dimension `findingDerivation` block in schema/framework-rubric.json, `interpretation: true`, one rationale per rule, read in written order with an unconditional last rule as the class fallback. The rubric loader refuses a rule that scores out of range, names an attribute the finding cannot carry, or sits after an unconditional rule for the same class (unreachable). Conditions reuse the existing tiny grammar over `severityRank` plus the finding's metrics; booleans are readable as `isStatic` and as `isStatic == 0`, so the negative needs no `!` operator.

DELIBERATE CALL, please review: none of the three detectors licenses a measured 0. Each one's blind spot is its own dimension's lowest bracket — HS-03 measures the admin surface, not autonomy (a hook that recomputes a fee from its own state inside beforeSwap is the 3 bracket and fires nothing); HS-05 only looks inside the swap path, while "one trusted dependency read outside the swap path" is the framework's 1 bracket; HS-06 only reports a fee it can show is unbounded, so a fee within a ceiling (bracket 2) fires nothing. All three therefore carry an `unmeasuredWhenSilent` reason. The pass buys the positive direction (three dimensions that could never be measured now can be), not permission to read silence as zero. Two further interpretations are argued in the rubric and flagged in notes-T.md: owner-only → 1 contradicts the framework's own 0 bracket ("all parameters set by an explicit privileged call") and is defended as a floor; HS-06 → 2 is one bracket below its own title because its evidence is negative.

HARNESS AS A COVERAGE SOURCE: CLASS_COVERAGE maps both new classes to ["harness"], and `enginesThatLooked` takes an optional harness summary — status ok adds `harness` to `looked`, failed records a declination with the revert quoted, skipped does neither. DeriveOptions.harness is structural ({status, reason?}) so derive.ts does not import manifest.ts. The CLI must pass it and must score after reconcileLayers (see integrator_changes).

SCHEMA: findings[].ruleClass enum + 2; findings[].engines[].engine documented as unconstrained with `harness` and the three probe rule names as examples; permissions.harnessRun.probes (eoaGuard per callback, exclusivity, optional exclusivityReason, selectors per callback) added strictly — unknown keys and unknown verdicts both fail; findings[].metrics no longer described as profile-only.

REPORT/SARIF: RULE_ID gains P-01 unvalidated-pool-key and P-02 callback-selector-mismatch (own series: the probe layer saw them); shortTitle covers all five classes; RULE_HELP gains the two entries and sharper HS-03/05/06 text; harness-sourced findings render as "Observed by the differential harness running the hook (`harness/selector-probe`)." and, when both layers carry one finding, "…, and reported from source by `hookrisk/…`."

DOCS: SCORING.md (shape-dependent scores table, why none of the three measures a zero, the harness as a coverage source, updated nine-dimension table); PRIOR_ART.md (Hacken article + checker rewritten, naming the three adopted checks and how hookrisk's differ; new hookguard section with what was taken, what was refused and the ~17%-of-busy-off-registry-hooks-publish-source ceiling); RESUME.md (reversed permission-bit landmine as a design constraint, a Deployed mode design subsection, a fourth-pass section, rewritten open items); notes-T.md.
